x: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885, when its first session met at Bombay under W.C. Bonnerjee. 1905 is the Partition of Bengal and 1906 the founding of the Muslim League.
t: Recall the founding year of the INC.

x: A.O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, helped found the INC in 1885 and served as its General Secretary. W.C. Bonnerjee was its first President, not its secretary.
t: Discriminate the founder-secretary from the first President.

x: Option A is incorrect: in its early years the Congress deliberately kept social reform issues off its platform to avoid division. National unity, removing caste, sectarian and regional biases, and formulating public demands were genuine early aims.
t: Recall what the early Congress avoided discussing.

x: Option C is incorrect: the first session was held at Bombay, not Calcutta. It met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College from 28 to 30 December 1885 with 72 delegates.
t: Check the place of the first session.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Swaraj was adopted as the goal at the 1906 Calcutta Session presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, but presiding or a flag does not cause the adoption. The flag detail in R is historically doubtful.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the 1929 Lahore Session under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted Purna Swaraj, and so 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day across the country.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: W.C. Bonnerjee presided at Bombay in 1885, Gokhale at Benares in 1905, Rash Behari Ghosh at Surat in 1907 and Ambika Charan Mazumdar at Lucknow in 1916, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.
t: Recall the president of each session.

x: Motilal Nehru presided at Calcutta in 1928, Jawaharlal Nehru at Lahore in 1929, Vallabhbhai Patel at Karachi in 1931 and Subhas Chandra Bose at Haripura in 1938, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the president of each session.

x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided at Faizpur in 1936, Subhas Bose at Tripuri in 1939, Abul Kalam Azad at Ramgarh in 1940 and Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Jaipur in 1948, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the president of each session.

x: I, II and III are correct: the Surat Split was in 1907, the Extremists returned at Lucknow in 1916, and Tilak last attended at Amritsar in 1919. IV is false because the 1927 Madras Session opposed the use of Indian troops in imperial wars.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: Karachi 1931 adopted the Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme resolution, Faizpur 1936 was the first rural session, Haripura 1938 was the 51st session and Jaipur 1948 the 55th.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: J.B. Kripalani was Congress President in 1947 at Independence, and Abul Kalam Azad held the presidency from the 1940 Ramgarh session until 1946.
t: Recall who was President in each period.

x: Surat was held in 1907, Lahore in 1929, Karachi in 1931 and Haripura in 1938, giving the order B, A, C, D.
t: Arrange the sessions by year.

x: All four are correct: Annie Besant was the first woman President (1917), Sarojini Naidu the first Indian woman President (1925), Faizpur (1936) the first rural session, and Belgaum (1924) the only session Gandhi presided over.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The first INC session met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, from 28 to 30 December 1885. The 1886 and 1938 dates are distractors from later sessions.
t: Recall the exact dates of the first session.

x: Both are true: separation of the Executive from the Judiciary was among the early Moderate demands, and formulating and presenting public demands to the government was one of the founding objectives of the Congress.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The item is doubtful: Dadabhai Naoroji presided three times, in 1886 (Calcutta), 1893 (Lahore) and 1906 (Calcutta), so both 1886 and 1893 fit. The key gives 1893, the Lahore session.
t: Recall all three Naoroji presidencies.

x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the 1905 Benares Session and voiced the Swadeshi and self-government demand there. The item is doubtful, since the formal call for Swaraj is usually credited to Dadabhai Naoroji at Calcutta in 1906.
t: Link the 1905 session to its President.

x: The Swaraj demand and flag belong to 1906, the Surat Split to 1907, the Lucknow Pact to 1916 and the Nehru Report to 1928, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the year of each event.

x: Option C is incorrect: the 1907 Surat Session split the Congress into Moderates (Naram Dal) and Extremists (Garam Dal); it did not reunite them. The reunion came only at Lucknow in 1916.
t: Discriminate the split of 1907 from the reunion of 1916.

x: The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938 during Subhas Chandra Bose's presidency, with Jawaharlal Nehru as Chairman and K.T. Shah as Secretary, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the role of each person in the committee.

x: Option A is incorrect: Bose was re-elected at Tripuri in 1939, but opposition from the Gandhian group forced him to resign; he then formed the Forward Bloc. The other statements are right.
t: Recall the outcome of the Tripuri crisis.

x: A is true: Gandhi gave up his primary membership of the Congress in 1934. B is false because he never formally rejoined and was not a member at Independence, though he remained its guiding leader.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: the Haripura Session met in Gujarat in February 1938 under Subhas Bose, and the Jaipur Session met in December 1948 under Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: Gandhi presided at Belgaum in 1924, Subhas Bose at Haripura in 1938, Abul Kalam Azad at Ramgarh in 1940 and Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Jaipur in 1948.
t: Check the president of each session.

x: The Gandhi–Irwin Pact of March 1931 suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement, and the Karachi Session that month endorsed it. The Lucknow Pact, Surat Split and Nehru Report belong to earlier years.
t: Recall the event just before March 1931.

x: The Haripura Session was held in Gujarat from 19 to 21 February 1938 under Subhas Chandra Bose. The other options shift the month, day or year.
t: Recall the exact dates of the Haripura Session.

x: Option D is incorrect: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the 55th session at Jaipur in December 1948. J.B. Kripalani was President in 1946–47.
t: Discriminate the 1946 President from the 1948 President.

x: W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session at Bombay in 1885. Dadabhai Naoroji presided in 1886, Badruddin Tyabji in 1887 and Alfred Webb in 1894.
t: Recall the first INC President.

x: Option C is incorrect: Rahimtulla M. Sayani, who presided at Calcutta in 1896, was the second Muslim President. Badruddin Tyabji, President at Madras in 1887, was the first.
t: Discriminate the first Muslim President from the second.

x: Dadabhai Naoroji presided at Calcutta in 1886, Alfred Webb at Madras in 1894, Rahimtulla Sayani at Calcutta in 1896 and Gokhale at Benares in 1905, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the president of each session.

x: Annie Besant, the Irish theosophist and Home Rule leader, was the first woman President at Calcutta in 1917. Sarojini Naidu, in 1925, was the first Indian woman President.
t: Discriminate the first woman from the first Indian woman President.

x: Motilal Nehru presided at Amritsar in 1919, C. Vijayaraghavachariar at Nagpur in 1920, C.R. Das at Gaya in 1922 and Gandhi at Belgaum in 1924, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the president of each session.

x: All three are correct: the Karachi Session of 1931 adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution, Nehru presided at Lucknow in April 1936, and Faizpur in December 1936 was the first rural session.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Haripura Session in 1938, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad presided over the Ramgarh Session in 1940.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Abul Kalam Azad presided at Ramgarh in 1940, J.B. Kripalani held the presidency in 1946, Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided at Jaipur in 1948 and Subhas Bose at Tripuri in 1939, giving a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii.
t: Recall the president for each year.

x: Calcutta was held in 1928, Lahore in 1929, Karachi in 1931 and Faizpur in 1936, giving the order A, C, B, D.
t: Arrange the sessions by year.

x: Benares 1905 met amid the Swadeshi movement, Calcutta 1906 adopted Swaraj, Surat 1907 saw the split, and Lucknow 1916 produced the Lucknow Pact, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the key event of each session.

x: Amritsar 1919 met after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, Kanpur 1925 had Sarojini Naidu as the first Indian woman President, Calcutta 1928 debated the Nehru Report, and Ramgarh 1940 had Azad as President, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the key feature of each session.

x: Both are true and R explains A: J.B. Kripalani became Congress President in 1946 and held the post through Independence in 1947, which is why he is linked with the presidency at that time.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Bombay hosted the 1885 session, Calcutta 1886 was the second session, Madras 1894 is linked to a European President (Alfred Webb), and Rash Behari Ghosh presided at Surat in 1907, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii. The item is doubtful: George Yule (1888) was the first European President.
t: Match each session by elimination.

x: Both are true: Ambika Charan Mazumdar presided over the 1916 Lucknow Session, and the 1917 session met at Calcutta under Annie Besant.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The 1922 Gaya Session under C.R. Das rejected council entry, after which Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party. Non-Cooperation was accepted in 1920, the Nehru Report came in 1928 and Purna Swaraj in 1929.
t: Link the 1922 session to the Swaraj Party.

x: Motilal Nehru presided at Calcutta in 1928, Patel at Karachi in 1931, the 1936 Lucknow entry is the plain "Congress session", and Nehru is matched to Faizpur 1936, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii. The item is doubtful because Nehru presided at both Lucknow and Faizpur in 1936.
t: Match the unique pairs first, then eliminate.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Bose was re-elected at Tripuri in 1939 by defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, and he resigned later that year. A later resignation cannot cause an earlier re-election.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Surendranath Banerjee led the Moderates who left the Congress in 1918 to form the Indian National Liberal Federation, along with Tej Bahadur Sapru and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri. Tilak and Lajpat Rai were Extremists, and Naoroji had died in 1917.
t: Discriminate the Moderate leaders from the Extremists.

x: Option B is incorrect: the Moderates wanted gradual reform through petitions, while the Extremists demanded more immediate Swaraj. The Moderate phase was 1885–1905, and the Extremists distrusted British rule and used agitation.
t: Discriminate Moderate aims from Extremist aims.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Dadabhai Naoroji's Drain Theory showed how British rule drained India's wealth, and this economic critique is the basis of his economic nationalism.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: M.G. Ranade combined social reform with Moderate nationalism, and both stressed slow, step-by-step change, which is why he is linked with gradual reform.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Tej Bahadur Sapru led the Indian National Liberal Federation, which chose constitutional cooperation with the British over mass agitation.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Dadabhai Naoroji gave the Drain Theory, Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society, Pherozeshah Mehta was a leading Moderate, and Surendranath Banerjee helped form the Liberal Federation, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the contribution of each leader.

x: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society at Poona in 1905, and Banerjee, Sastri and Sapru were all Liberal leaders. The key gives a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii, but the item is doubtful because "Liberal Federation" and "Indian National Liberal Federation" are the same body.
t: Match the unique pair first, then eliminate.

x: I and II are correct: the Extremists stood for assertive nationalism and relied on agitation and mass mobilisation. III is false because gradual reform was the Moderate approach.
t: Discriminate Extremist methods from Moderate methods.

x: I and II are correct: the Moderates used constitutional methods and drew little on mass politics. III is false because they began with faith in British justice; growing distrust marked the Extremists.
t: Discriminate Moderate attitudes from Extremist attitudes.

x: Both are true: Surendranath Banerjee and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri were Moderate leaders who later led the Liberal Federation.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: A is true: the 1906 Calcutta Session under Naoroji adopted Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education. B is false because Surat 1907 is remembered for the Moderate–Extremist split, not as a meeting of Moderate constitutionalists.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Servants of India Society came in 1905, the Calcutta Session in 1906, the Surat Session in 1907 and the Liberal Federation in 1918, giving the order C, D, A, B.
t: Arrange the events by year.

x: Three are Moderates or Liberals: Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Tej Bahadur Sapru. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Extremist leader.
t: Discriminate Moderate leaders from Extremist leaders.

x: Both are true: the Moderates relied on petitions, prayers and persuasion, and Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the 1906 Calcutta Session.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The first session met at Bombay in December 1885 under W.C. Bonnerjee. Calcutta 1886 and 1906 were Naoroji's sessions, and Benares 1905 was Gokhale's.
t: Recall the year and place of the first session.

x: Option B is incorrect: Swadeshi-era nationalism belongs to the 1905 Benares session, not 1886. The second session was held at Calcutta in 1886 under Dadabhai Naoroji.
t: Discriminate the 1886 session from the 1905 session.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the 1905 session was held at Benares under Gokhale, but the Swadeshi spirit came from the Partition of Bengal, not from the venue or the President.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: the 1906 Calcutta Session under Dadabhai Naoroji passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Surat 1907 saw the Moderate–Extremist split, Lucknow 1916 the Lucknow Pact and the Extremists' return, Amritsar 1919 followed Jallianwala Bagh, and Nagpur 1920 reorganised the Congress and adopted Non-Cooperation, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the key event of each session.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the 1927 session met at Madras under M.A. Ansari, but the Simon Commission boycott came from the all-British membership of the Commission, not from the venue or President.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: the 1928 Calcutta Session under Motilal Nehru backed the Nehru Report and gave the British a one-year ultimatum to accept Dominion Status.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: Nehru presided at Lahore in 1929 (Purna Swaraj), Patel at Karachi in 1931 (Fundamental Rights and Economic Programme), and Rajendra Prasad at Bombay in 1934.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The 1936 Faizpur session in Maharashtra, under Jawaharlal Nehru, was the first Congress session held in a village. Haripura in 1938 was the second rural session.
t: Discriminate Faizpur from Haripura.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the 1939 session was held at Tripuri under Bose, but the conflict came from Gandhi's group opposing Bose's re-election, not from the venue.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: J.B. Kripalani presided over the Meerut session of November 1946, the last before Independence. Azad was President from 1940 to 1946, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided after Independence, in 1948.
t: Recall the last pre-Independence President.

x: Bombay was held in 1885, Calcutta in 1906, Lahore in 1929 and Jaipur in 1948, giving the order B, C, A, D.
t: Arrange the sessions by year.

x: Two were presided over by Nehru: Lahore 1929 and Faizpur 1936. Karachi 1931 was under Vallabhbhai Patel and Haripura 1938 under Subhas Chandra Bose.
t: Check the president of each session.

x: Bose presided at Haripura in 1938 and Tripuri in 1939, Azad at Ramgarh in 1940 and Kripalani at Meerut in 1946. The code pairs items in order when List-II repeats, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the president of each session.

x: All four are correct: Belgaum 1924 was Gandhi's only presidency, Kanpur 1925 had Sarojini Naidu, Faizpur 1936 was the first rural session, and Jaipur 1948 met after Independence.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Jaipur session was post-Independence because it met in December 1948, after August 1947, not because Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938, after the Haripura session, under Congress President Subhas Chandra Bose, with Nehru as Chairman.
t: Link the committee to Bose's 1938 presidency.

x: Ambika Charan Majumdar presided over the 1916 Lucknow Session, where the Congress and the Muslim League signed the Lucknow Pact. Motilal Nehru, Jawaharlal Nehru and Patel presided at later sessions.
t: Recall the President of the 1916 session.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Complete Independence became the Congress goal in 1929 because the Lahore Session under Jawaharlal Nehru passed the Purna Swaraj Resolution.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi at Lahore at midnight on 31 December 1929. 26 January 1930 was the later Purna Swaraj Day.
t: Discriminate the flag hoisting from Purna Swaraj Day.

x: Both are true: after the Lahore resolution of December 1929, the Congress observed 26 January 1930 as Purna Swaraj Day across India.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: the Karachi Session of 1931 adopted Fundamental Rights covering civil liberties, equality and citizens' rights, along with an Economic Programme for labour welfare and worker protection.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Majumdar presided at Lucknow in 1916, Motilal Nehru wrote the Nehru Report, Annie Besant led the Home Rule Movement and presided in 1917, and Patel presided at Karachi in 1931, giving a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Recall the event linked to each leader.

x: The Swadeshi and Boycott movement against the 1905 Partition of Bengal boycotted foreign goods and promoted Indian goods and national education. Complete Independence and the Nehru Report came in the late 1920s.
t: Link the movement to the Partition of Bengal.

x: Annie Besant led the Home Rule League and presided over the Calcutta Session in 1917. Majumdar presided in 1916, Motilal Nehru in 1919 and 1928, and Patel in 1931.
t: Recall the 1917 Congress President.

x: All three are correct: the Congress–League pact was signed at Lucknow in 1916, Motilal Nehru chaired the Nehru Report committee, and Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Patel presided at Karachi in 1931 and Nehru drafted its Fundamental Rights resolution, but the drafting does not explain who was President.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The Congress–League pact was signed in 1916, the Nehru Report in 1928, the Purna Swaraj Resolution in 1929 and Purna Swaraj Day was 26 January 1930, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall the year of each event.

x: 26 January 1930, Purna Swaraj Day, was observed as Independence Day. The date was later chosen for the Constitution to come into force in 1950.
t: Recall what 26 January 1930 was called.

x: All four are correct: Majumdar presided at Lucknow in 1916, Motilal Nehru wrote the 1928 Nehru Report, Annie Besant led the Home Rule Movement, and Patel presided at Karachi in 1931.
t: Check each pair separately.

x: Lucknow was held in 1916, Calcutta (the Nehru Report ultimatum) in 1928, Lahore in 1929 and Karachi in 1931, giving the order B, D, C, A.
t: Arrange the sessions by year.

x: Both are true: the Nehru Report of 1928, drafted for the All-Parties Conference, was an Indian-made constitutional framework proposing Dominion Status.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Fundamental Rights covered civil liberties, the Economic Programme covered labour welfare, Purna Swaraj meant Complete Independence, and Swadeshi meant boycotting foreign goods, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the content of each resolution or movement.

x: The 1928 Calcutta Session gave the British one year to accept the Nehru Report; otherwise the Congress would launch a mass movement. When the year passed, this led to Purna Swaraj and Civil Disobedience.
t: Recall the terms of the 1928 ultimatum.

x: Both are true: the Karachi Fundamental Rights resolution guaranteed equality and freedoms, and its Economic Programme made the state responsible for labour welfare and key industries.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Karachi Economic Programme of 1931 made the state responsible for labour welfare and worker protection. The Nehru Report ultimatum, the Swadeshi boycott and Complete Independence belong to other events.
t: Link each option to its own event.

x: Jawaharlal Nehru, President of the 1929 Lahore Session, hoisted the flag on the Ravi and declared Complete Independence. Motilal Nehru had presided in 1928.
t: Discriminate Jawaharlal Nehru from Motilal Nehru.
